source.section: TC-40 lines 4 to 22 (Instructions PDF p.9 Line 4; PDF p.10 Lines 5 to 20 and the Line 17 table; PDF p.11 Line 22); Line 21 and Qualified Exempt Taxpayer Worksheet lines 1 to 5 (PDF pp.10-11)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 21,000.00 = 21,000.00. Federal taxable income = 21,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 - 1 x 2,000 age 65 additional = 3,250.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Utah starts from federal AGI). TC-40 (single): line 4 federal AGI 21,000.00. Line 5 additions: none, 0.00. Line 6 = 21,000.00 + 0.00 = 21,000.00. Line 7 state tax refund 0.00. Line 8 subtractions 0.00. Line 9 Utah taxable income = 21,000.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 21,000.00. Line 10 = 21,000.00 x 0.045 = 945.00. Lines 11 to 16, by the projection: no dependents; the deduction on line 12 is held as the cap 15,750.00; initial credit = 0.06 x min(line 9 21,000.00, cap 15,750.00) = 0.06 x 15,750.00 = 945.00. The form's line 12 takes federal line 12e, 17,750.00 with the age 65 additional, so its line 16 is 1,065.00, line 20 1,028.77; the expected figures follow the projection's cap. Line 17 base phase-out amount 18,213.00. Line 18 = max(0, 21,000.00 - 18,213.00) = 2,787.00. Line 19 = 2,787.00 x 0.013 = 36.231. Line 20 = max(0, 945.00 - 36.231) = 908.769. Line 21 worksheet: line 1 federal AGI 21,000.00; line 2 standard deduction 15,750.00; line 3 senior deduction 0.00 (no amount in Utah's sources); line 4 15,750.00; line 5 = max(0, 21,000.00 - 15,750.00) = 5,250.00. Line 5 is above zero, so not exempt; line 21 blank. Line 22 and TC-40A Part 3: line 20 908.769 = 908.769; credits 908.77. Tax = 945.00 - 908.77 = 36.23. The form, with line 12 at federal 12e, gives tax 0.00; expected follows the projection. Federal AGI is within the reach of Schedule 1-A line 37 (the worksheet's line 3), which Utah's sources print no amount for and the projection leaves out; with enough of that deduction the true tax is 0. Over the threshold by the projection, which holds the standard deduction only. Expected lines are the formula results rounded to the cent at the end (half up); the three-decimal figures above are unrounded.
accepted_approximations: Utah has no deduction from income, so base.deductions is empty on purpose. The taxpayer tax credit stands in for it: 6% of the capped income, cap = the federal standard deduction for the status, so the credit is 945 single, 1,417.50 head of household, 1,890 joint or qualifying surviving spouse, once income reaches the cap. Below the cap the credit is smaller than the form's, but 6% of income exceeds 4.5% tax either way, so tax is 0 on both. The phase-out (line 19) comes off the credit, after the 6%, as it does after the 4.5% on the Social Security credit. The cap leaves out the federal age 65 and blindness extras, which line 12 includes because it takes federal line 12e; the Utah sources print no amount for them.

The Qualified Exempt Taxpayer threshold is the standard deduction only. The worksheet adds the federal enhanced deduction for seniors (Schedule 1-A line 37), which the Utah sources print no amount for and the format can't hold.
